about.title: About This Project
about.p1: This project, available at vathra.xyz, is a digital initiative dedicated to mapping and documenting the status of the Hellenic Army Geographical Service (ΓΥΣ) trigonometric points across Greece.
about.visionP1: Many of these historical points are now forgotten, damaged, or lost to time. Our mission is to create a living, crowd-sourced archive to preserve this heritage. By combining official public data with on-the-ground reports from a community of users, we aspire to:
about.visionL1: Build the most complete and up-to-date public record of the status of these points.
about.visionL2: Foster a community of explorers—hikers, surveyors, and historians—to actively contribute to this effort.
about.visionL3: Provide a valuable, open-access resource for research, education, and recreation.
about.doiP1: To ensure long-term preservation, the dataset is periodically archived at Zenodo.
about.doiLinkText: The latest version is available at Zenodo with DOI:
about.codeP1: The application's code is open source, licensed under the AGPLv3. Contributions are welcome at our GitHub repository.
about.contentP1: All user-submitted content is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike (CC BY-SA).
about.paperP1: The platform's architecture, empirical results, and legal framework are described in a preprint published on EarthArXiv.

about.exportP1: Download the full dataset of trigonometric points in your preferred format. CSV can be opened in Excel or QGIS, KML works with Google Earth and most GIS software.
about.supportP1: vathra.xyz is a volunteer-run, self-funded project. If you find it useful, consider supporting its development and infrastructure costs.
about.communityP1: Join our Discord server to discuss the project, share discoveries, and connect with other contributors.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.introP1: vathra.xyz ("we", "us", or "our") is a volunteer-run, open-source project dedicated to mapping trigonometric survey points in Greece. This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, and protect your personal information when you use our service.
privacy.dataCollectedP1: We collect the following information when you sign in:
privacy.dataCollectedL1: Google account information: your name, email address, and profile picture (when signing in with Google).
privacy.dataCollectedL2: Passkey credentials: public key identifiers (when signing in with a passkey). No passwords are stored.
privacy.dataCollectedL3: User-submitted content: status reports, comments, and photos you voluntarily submit about trigonometric points.
privacy.dataCollectedL4: Session data: a session cookie to keep you signed in. No third-party tracking cookies are used.
privacy.howWeUseP1: We use the information we collect to:
privacy.howWeUseL1: Authenticate you and maintain your session.
privacy.howWeUseL2: Display your name and profile picture alongside your reports and on your public profile.
privacy.howWeUseL3: Operate, maintain, and improve the service.
privacy.thirdPartyP1: We use the following third-party services to operate vathra.xyz:
privacy.thirdPartyL1: Google OAuth: for authentication. Google's privacy policy applies to data processed by Google during sign-in.
privacy.thirdPartyL2: Cloudflare: for content delivery, image hosting, and map tile serving.
privacy.thirdPartyL3: Sentry: for error tracking and application monitoring. Error reports may include anonymized technical data.
privacy.cookiesP1: We use a single essential session cookie to keep you signed in. We do not use advertising, analytics, or third-party tracking cookies.
privacy.retentionP1: Your account and reports are retained for as long as you maintain your account. You may request deletion of your account and associated data at any time by contacting us.
privacy.rightsL1: Access the personal data we hold about you.
privacy.rightsL2: Request correction or deletion of your personal data.
privacy.rightsL3: Request export of your data in a portable format.
privacy.contactP1: For privacy-related inquiries, contact us at

terms.accountsP1: You may sign in using Google OAuth or a passkey. You are responsible for maintaining the security of your account. You must provide accurate information and must not impersonate others.
